title_vi: Người đàn bà có con chó nhỏ
translation_direction: ru → vi; direct from the specifically identified complete Russian electronic witness
ai_disclosure: Direct AI-produced Vietnamese prose by Claude Opus 5.5. The drafting system conducted the final full assessment; a separate-context assessment by the same model family read every pair and supplied findings first. No human translator, editor, reviewer, independent model consensus or actual reader feedback is recorded.

entry_conditions: Complete named-source and Vietnamese texts, explicit alignment and exact content hashes.
Compare every source and target passage; disclose that this assessor also revised the text and has seen earlier AI assessments.
Source and target edition titles are present and compared explicitly; the title review must match both catalog title strings exactly.
exit_conditions: One complete AI review with a weighted score at least 8.6 using the five unchanged weights and half-point category scores; no separate numerical dimension floors.
All canonical passages reviewed; no unresolved major or critical finding; source and target hashes match the final text.
Publication and rights status are recorded separately in the edition catalog; an AI score does not supply a license.
The selected review includes source_title, target_title and a substantive title rationale; changed titles require a fresh matching review.
review_process.human_feedback: Optional after publication or while a work remains a draft; no prior human publication review is required by v2.

decisions.decision: Gurov uses tôi/cô, then anh/em after he moves to ты (2.15); Anna keeps tôi/anh while she uses вы and becomes em/anh when she uses ты (4.8). Gurov’s theatre вы (3.35) is tôi with no second-person pronoun.
decisions.rationale: The shifts in address are part of Chekhov’s portrayal of intimacy and distance.

revision_history.scope: Complete initial direct translation, separate-context full source/target assessment and concrete revisions before the selected final review.

changes.explanation: серое платье had become a Vietnamese áo dài; now chiếc váy xám, preserving the grey motif without a cultural transplant.
трогательна means touching/pitiable, not moved: trông thật đáng thương, khiến người ta mủi lòng.
жизнь сложилась is ‘turned out’, not that life arranged things: thành ra buồn thảm.
лакей unified as tên đầy tớ in 2.18 and 3.27, with лакейски-скромное as khúm núm; the badge is a university graduate’s badge.
Gurov’s formal вы in the theatre no longer carries intimate em.
набережная rendered as the promenade (đường dạo ven biển) in 1.1, 2.25 and 2.34.
The two-lives passage: neutral đầy những, hạt nhân for зерно, giấu kín mọi người, khắc khoải lo toan.

selection_limit: Chosen for a complete, directly sourced and openly reusable Vietnamese edition. Existing Vietnamese translations, their quality and reader demand have not been comprehensively assessed; no absence or superiority claim is made.

glossary.draft_rendering: người đàn bà có con chó nhỏ
glossary.rationale: The established Vietnamese title, used identically at each recurrence of the nickname.
Gurov’s cynical formula recurs and is listed again among the lies of his public life.
One rendering for Anna’s insult and the narrator’s later view of the husband, including the badge ‘like a lackey’s number’.
The Yalta promenade where people parade and watch, not merely the shore.

witness_decision: Selected the Russian Wikisource transcription marked 100% quality, whose stated source is the FEB electronic text of А. П. Чехов, Полное собрание сочинений и писем в 30 т., Сочинения т. 10, pp. 128–143 (Москва: Наука). First published in Русская мысль, 1899, no. 12; the 1899 journal text and the 1903 Marks edition were not collated. Wikisource’s own explanatory notes are excluded.

unresolved_questions.explanation: The orthographic joke about not writing ъ requires knowledge of the Russian spelling reform; it is kept without a gloss.

title_review.target_title: Người đàn bà có con chó nhỏ
title_review.rationale: Người đàn bà có con chó nhỏ is the established Vietnamese title, matches the nickname used in the text and renders the diminutive собачка.

passage_assessment_notes.assessment: Compared chapter I: Yalta, Gurov’s marriage and cynicism, the first meeting and his first impression.
Compared chapter II: the pier, the first night, the watermelon, the confession, Oreanda, the summer and the parting.
Compared chapter III: Moscow, memory, the sturgeon, S., the fence, the theatre and the staircase.
Compared chapter IV: the Moscow meetings, the two lives, the mirror, love at last and the unresolved ending.
